hunt.justification: SCKit represents a direct threat to the trust relationship between MSPs and their customers. By abusing legitimate remote-access tools to hijack technician sessions, the threat actor can achieve broad lateral movement that bypasses standard perimeter controls.

scenario.summary: Threat actors abuse vulnerabilities in ScreenConnect server extensions or hijacked management consoles to deploy unauthorized remote-access clients and the SCKit malware toolkit. The campaign establishes long-term persistence on customer endpoints to host RelayTrap, a component that targets IT technicians' workstations with malicious payloads during support sessions.

meta.rationale: The scoping query targets the vulnerability used for initial access. The hunt also checks all hosts for persistence regardless of patch status to identify infections that occurred before patching.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder who has compromised a ScreenConnect client is maintaining access via script-based Registry persistence and is using the RelayTrap component to target connecting technician sessions.

hunt.name: SCKit Persistence and RelayTrap Targeting
hunt.description: This hunt identifies long-term SCKit infections following the abuse of ScreenConnect clients. It begins by scoping the estate to endpoints running unpatched or vulnerable ScreenConnect clients (CVE-2026-84869). It then executes a fan-out to find independent evidence of the toolkit's presence: rare batch or PowerShell scripts persisting in Registry Run keys, the execution of named SCKit artifacts like TrapWatch or Lite-Alert, and network communication with known malicious relay infrastructure. An agent triages these signals to identify compromised customer endpoints that may be attempting to hijack technician sessions.

nodes.label: Rare script persistence in Run keys

config.content: SELECT LOWER(reg_value_data) AS script_data, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_count, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_registry_activity WHERE (LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\currentversion\run%' OR LOWER(reg_target) LIKE '%\currentversion\runonce%') AND (LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%.bat%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%.ps1%' OR LOWER(reg_value_data) LIKE '%.cmd%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY 1 HAVING host_count <= 3 ORDER BY host_count ASC
config.description: Identify hosts where SCKit launchers or cleanup scripts (Stop-LabTrap.bat) have been added to registry startup keys.
config.expected_signal: Rare scripts (batch or PowerShell) persisting in Run keys. Malicious launchers like Run-Lateral-Full.bat will appear as unique entries.

config.objective: Determine which hosts are compromised by SCKit. A host is 'malicious' if it shows either artifact execution (TrapWatch/RelayTrap) or a combination of vulnerability (CVE-2026-84869) and rare script-based Run key persistence. Evaluate if the host process names suggest a technician workstation was the source of DNS lookups to the relays.
